column1: # Programs that must NOT assemble — task B-044.
# AUTHORED, not generated, and the expectations here are OURS. Every other
# corpus in this directory compares against riscv64-elf-as, which cannot help
# with rejection: an assembler that refuses a program tells you nothing about
# what OUR diagnostic should say, and GNU as has no opinion on a kāraka sigil.
# So this file is a different kind of check. It does not ask "are the bytes
# right" but "does the wrong program fail, and does it fail legibly". Both
# halves matter. Every defect found in this assembler so far — the conjunct
# sigil, the shift-immediate opcodes, every load assembling as `lb` — produced
# a VALID instruction that nobody asked for, which is the failure mode a
# byte-comparison corpus catches only where it happens to look.
# Columns: sassembly, a fragment the message must contain, why it is wrong.

column3: why
B-044: silently encoded a store of register 7 — t0 (5) OR sp (2)
the same sigil that corrupts a store happened to work here; both are rejected
two destinations — the parser catches this one before the encoder does
two values and no address to store them to
5000 does not fit the 12 bits addi gives it
a verb with one argument where three are needed
the sentence never ends
R-02-1: an instruction absent from the registry cannot be written
a name ending in म् is read as an operand, not a verb (ADR-0004)
an operand with no case marking has no role
128 is not a width the ISA has
a pseudo-instruction is named but has no encoding of its own
B-075: a conversion names what it writes AND what it reads; one type leaves eighteen encodings fitting and file order choosing
B-075: there is no 16-bit float to convert from, and a pair that does not exist must not fall back to one that does
B-075: only a conversion reads one type and writes another
B-067: a doubled इति is the word itself, so nothing closes this string
B-067: content after the closing इति would assemble as `क`, which is not what the program says
ADR-0044 D3: a Devanagari-8 body is one word of letters; a space between two does not pack to one octet each
ADR-0044 D3: U+1CD0 is in R-15-1's repertoire but outside U+0900–U+097F, so it has no Devanagari-8 octet
ADR-0044 D3: the opener mirrors उक्तम् and nothing closed it
ADR-0044 D3: content after the close, refused as for उक्तम्
B-077: भ names a float and योगः adds integers; the letter was validated and discarded, so this assembled as addw
B-077: the corpus wrote every float family with the integer type that happens to share its width
ADR-0012: this assembled for 150 cycles, and the claim that a directive is tellable from an instruction without knowing the names was false while it did
a lone ॥ was silently an empty statement; a mark that assembles to nothing is how a typo becomes a program that says nothing
an opened and closed directive that names nothing
ADR-0013: an address is 64 bits, and four bytes would keep the low half and discard the rest
ADR-0014: sra shifts an i64, so calling its operands unsigned contradicts the name ADR-0006 gave it
B-101: this assembled to lwu, which zero-extends, while its own type suffix said signed
